title: Pass 4: Psychological and Behavioral Signals
description: Extracts psychological and behavioral signals from a conversation. All items use the evidence_item format to enforce the evidence-over-inference principle.

dominant_affect.description: Primary emotional tones present in the conversation.

energy_level.description: Overall energy level of user engagement.

evidence.description: Verbatim quotes or precise turn references supporting the affect and energy assessment.

emotional_tone_and_energy.description: Dominant emotional tone and energy level of the conversation.

cognitive_style.description: How problems are approached: systematic, exploratory, analytical, intuitive, indecisive, etc.

communication_style.description: How requests are framed: directive, collaborative, exploratory, self-deprecating, etc.

behavioral_patterns.description: Observable patterns in how the user engages with the AI.

self_concept_signals.description: How the user describes or positions themselves.

motivation_and_reward_patterns.description: What seems to drive engagement and what the user finds rewarding.

epistemic_tier.description: How interpretive this framework-relevant signal is.

frameworks.description: Which personality frameworks this signal may be relevant to.

potential_indicators.description: What this signal might indicate within those frameworks (e.g. 'high openness', 'INTP preference for Ti', 'type 5 withdrawal').

evidence.description: Verbatim quotes or precise turn references supporting this signal.

disconfirming_evidence.description: Evidence that weakens or complicates the proposed interpretation.

framework_relevant_signals.description: Evidence that may later map to Big Five, MBTI, Enneagram, attachment style, or other recognized frameworks.

negative_space.description: Brief notes about why little or no psychological signal was extracted from the conversation.
